7.Labs

7.1Full project — web → menu-api → orders-db

Deploy three tiers with three Service types — NodePort for the entry, ClusterIP between services, Headless for the database — and follow one request through all of them.

▶Lab · one request through the whole stack

↔ swipe the diagram · ⤢ full screen
01Browser → NodePort
The user opens http://192.168.1.101:30080 (any node IP works).
← BackStep 1 / 7
02web-nodeport-service → a web pod
node-1's NodePort rule DNATs to a web pod — this time the local web-1.
Step 2 / 7
03nginx calls the API by Service name
web proxies /api to menu-api-service. DNS → 10.96.0.50.
Step 3 / 7
04menu-api-service → a menu-api pod
node-1's rules pick menu-api-2 on node-2; the packet crosses to node-2.
Step 4 / 7
05menu-api → PostgreSQL primary via headless DNS
Writes go to pod 0 of the StatefulSet: DNS returns the pod IP, no DNAT.
Step 5 / 7
06Data flows back
Each hop returns through its own conntrack entry.
Step 6 / 7
07What you built
Three Service types, each for its job. Every file follows below.
Step 7 / 7Next →

All files

📄 lab-full-stack.yamlSecret + Service + StatefulSet + Deployment + Service + Deployment + Service · Secret · Services · StatefulSet · Deployments
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: orders-db-secret
  namespace: jahez-prod
type: Opaque
stringData:
  password: change-me-in-aws-secrets-manager
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: orders-db-headless-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: orders-db
  # ② How is it reached? — no virtual IP: DNS returns pod IPs
  clusterIP: None
  ports:
    - # ② PostgreSQL
      name: postgres
      port: 5432
      targetPort: postgres
  # ④ What does DNS publish? — Ready pods only
  publishNotReadyAddresses: false
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: orders-db-stateful-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  serviceName: orders-db-headless-service   # ← gives each pod a DNS name
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16.4
          ports:
            - name: postgres
              containerPort: 5432
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: orders-db-secret
                  key: password
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
        storageClassName: gp3
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 50Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: menu-api-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: menu-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: menu-api                # ← the Service selector matches this label
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: menu-api
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/menu-api:1.14.2
          ports:
            - name: http             # ← targetPort: http points here
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:            # ← only Ready pods become endpoints
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          lifecycle:
            preStop:                 # ← drain before the endpoint is removed
              exec:
                command: ["sleep", "5"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-api-service           # DNS: menu-api-service.jahez-prod.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
spec:
  # ① Which pods receive the traffic?
  selector:
    app: menu-api
  # ② How is it reached?
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - # ② Which port do clients use, and where does it land?
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
      appProtocol: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
  # ③ Where does the traffic go?
  sessionAffinity: None
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  trafficDistribution: PreferSameZone
  # ④ What does DNS publish?
  publishNotReadyAddresses: false
  # ⑥ Which IP families?
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-deployment
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: ghcr.io/jahez/web:3.8.0
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: http
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: web
  # ② How is it reached? — the same port on every node
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - # ② client → node:30080 → Service :80 → pod :http (3000)
      name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
      nodePort: 30080
  # ③ Where does the traffic go?
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
⌘ Commands
kubectl apply -f lab-full-stack.yaml
create all three tiers
read YAML → send to API server → create / update object → controllers react
kubectl apply — create or update from YAML
-f — file (or folder / URL) with the YAML
kubectl rollout status statefulset/orders-db-stateful-set -n jahez-prod
wait for the database pods
read rollout status
kubectl rollout — manage rollouts
statefulset/orders-db-stateful-set — object of type statefulset named orders-db-stateful-set
-n — namespace to work in
kubectl get service,endpointslices -n jahez-prod
three Services, slices with Ready endpoints
ask API server → print objects
kubectl get — read objects
-n — namespace to work in
curl -s http://192.168.1.101:30080/
the whole chain from outside
runs locally / in the pod · nothing sent — cluster unchanged
curl — HTTP client — runs inside the pod, no API call
Expected output (example)
NAME                                 TYPE        CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)
service/menu-api-service             ClusterIP   10.96.0.50   <none>        80/TCP
service/orders-db-headless-service   ClusterIP   None         <none>        5432/TCP
service/web-nodeport-service         NodePort    10.96.0.21   <none>        80:30080/TCP

7.2CKAD tasks — with hidden solutions

Six CKAD-style tasks on the jahez-prod cluster. Try each one first, then open the solution.

Task 1 · Expose a Deployment

In namespace jahez-prod, create a ClusterIP Service order-api-service for order-api-deployment: port 80 → container port 8080.

Commands
kubectl expose deployment order-api-deployment --name=order-api-service --port=80 --target-port=8080 -n jahez-prod
📄 task1-order-api-service.yamlService
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: order-api-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: order-api
  # ② How is it reached?
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
Verify
kubectl get endpointslices -n jahez-prod -l kubernetes.io/service-name=order-api-service
kubectl run tmp -n jahez-prod --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- http://order-api-service/healthz
Expected output (example)
NAME                      ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
order-api-service-9qv4c   IPv4          8080    10.244.1.41,10.244.2.41,10.244.3.41
Exam traps: forget --name → the Service is called order-api-deployment · port vs target-port swapped · wrong namespace: always add -n

Task 2 · Fix a Service with no endpoints

menu-api-service resolves but every call is refused. Find and fix the cause without recreating the Service.

Commands
kubectl get endpointslices -n jahez-prod -l kubernetes.io/service-name=menu-api-service
kubectl get service menu-api-service -n jahez-prod -o wide   # SELECTOR app=menu-apl
kubectl get pods -n jahez-prod --show-labels | grep menu
kubectl patch service menu-api-service -n jahez-prod -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"menu-api"}}}'
📄 task2-menu-api-service.yamlService
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: menu-api-service           # DNS: menu-api-service.jahez-prod.svc.cluster.local
  namespace: jahez-prod
  labels:
    app: menu-api
spec:
  # ① Which pods receive the traffic?
  selector:
    app: menu-api
  # ② How is it reached?
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - # ② Which port do clients use, and where does it land?
      name: http
      protocol: TCP
      appProtocol: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
  # ③ Where does the traffic go?
  sessionAffinity: None
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  trafficDistribution: PreferSameZone
  # ④ What does DNS publish?
  publishNotReadyAddresses: false
  # ⑥ Which IP families?
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
Verify
kubectl get endpointslices -n jahez-prod -l kubernetes.io/service-name=menu-api-service
Expected output (example)
NAME                     ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
menu-api-service-x7k2p   IPv4          8080    10.244.1.20,10.244.2.20,10.244.3.20
Exam traps: check endpoints first, not DNS · the selector must match the pod template labels, not the Deployment's own labels · also check pods are Ready

Task 3 · NodePort on a fixed port

Expose web-deployment on every node at port 30080 → container port 3000, Service name web-nodeport-service.

Commands
kubectl create service nodeport web-nodeport-service --tcp=80:3000 --node-port=30080 -n jahez-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml > task3.yaml
# edit selector to app: web, then:
kubectl apply -f task3.yaml
📄 task3-web-nodeport-service.yamlService
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-nodeport-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: web
  # ② How is it reached? — same port on every node
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 3000
      nodePort: 30080
Verify
kubectl get service web-nodeport-service -n jahez-prod
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://192.168.1.101:30080/
Expected output (example)
NAME                   TYPE       CLUSTER-IP   EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)        AGE
web-nodeport-service   NodePort   10.96.0.21   <none>        80:30080/TCP   5s
200
Exam traps: create service nodeport sets selector app=web-nodeport-service — fix it · nodePort must be 30000–32767 and unused

Task 4 · Headless Service for a StatefulSet

Give each orders-db-stateful-set pod a stable DNS name via a Headless Service orders-db-headless-service on port 5432.

Commands
kubectl create service clusterip orders-db-headless-service --clusterip="None" --tcp=5432:5432 -n jahez-prod --dry-run=client -o yaml > task4.yaml
# set selector app: orders-db; StatefulSet serviceName: orders-db-headless-service
kubectl apply -f task4.yaml
📄 orders-db.yamlSecret + Service + StatefulSet
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: orders-db-secret
  namespace: jahez-prod
type: Opaque
stringData:
  password: change-me-in-aws-secrets-manager
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: orders-db-headless-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: orders-db
  # ② How is it reached? — no virtual IP: DNS returns pod IPs
  clusterIP: None
  ports:
    - # ② PostgreSQL
      name: postgres
      port: 5432
      targetPort: postgres
  # ④ What does DNS publish? — Ready pods only
  publishNotReadyAddresses: false
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: orders-db-stateful-set
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  serviceName: orders-db-headless-service   # ← gives each pod a DNS name
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: orders-db
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: orders-db
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:16.4
          ports:
            - name: postgres
              containerPort: 5432
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: orders-db-secret
                  key: password
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata:
        name: data
      spec:
        accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
        storageClassName: gp3
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: 50Gi
Verify
kubectl run tmp -n jahez-prod --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 -- nslookup orders-db-stateful-set-0.orders-db-headless-service
Expected output (example)
Name:   orders-db-stateful-set-0.orders-db-headless-service.jahez-prod.svc.cluster.local
Address: 10.244.1.30
Exam traps: serviceName must equal the Headless Service name · CLUSTER-IP must show None — you cannot change an existing ClusterIP Service to headless; recreate it

Task 5 · ExternalName alias

Pods must reach the payment provider as payment-gateway-service, which should resolve to api.checkout.com.

Commands
kubectl create service externalname payment-gateway-service --external-name=api.checkout.com -n jahez-prod
📄 payment-gateway-service.yamlService
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-gateway-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ② How is it reached? — a DNS alias, nothing else
  type: ExternalName
  # ④ What does DNS publish? — CNAME to this host
  externalName: api.checkout.com
Verify
kubectl run tmp -n jahez-prod --rm -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- dig +short payment-gateway-service.jahez-prod.svc.cluster.local
Expected output (example)
api.checkout.com.
<public IP>
Exam traps: externalName must be a hostname, not an IP · no ports are remapped

Task 6 · Wrong targetPort

report-export-service has endpoints but calls time out. The container listens on 8080. Fix it.

Commands
kubectl get endpointslices -n jahez-prod -l kubernetes.io/service-name=report-export-service   # PORTS 80?
kubectl get pod -n jahez-prod -l app=report-export -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.containers[0].ports}'
kubectl patch service report-export-service -n jahez-prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":8080}]'
📄 report-export-service.yamlService
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: report-export-service
  namespace: jahez-prod
spec:
  # ① Which pods?
  selector:
    app: report-export
  # ② How is it reached?
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  # ③ Where does the traffic go? — same client IP → same pod
  sessionAffinity: ClientIP
  sessionAffinityConfig:
    clientIP:
      timeoutSeconds: 1800
Verify
kubectl run tmp -n jahez-prod --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 -- wget -qO- http://report-export-service/healthz
Expected output (example)
ok
Exam traps: EndpointSlice PORTS shows the resolved pod port — the fastest clue · prefer a named targetPort so this cannot drift

7.3Cheat sheet

Create

kubectl expose deploy menu-api-deployment --name=menu-api-service --port=80 --target-port=http -n jahez-prod
kubectl create service clusterip x-service --tcp=80:8080 --dry-run=client -o yaml
kubectl create service nodeport x-service --tcp=80:3000 --node-port=30080
kubectl create service externalname x-service --external-name=api.checkout.com

Inspect

kubectl get svc -n jahez-prod -o wide
kubectl describe svc menu-api-service -n jahez-prod
kubectl get endpointslices -n jahez-prod -l kubernetes.io/service-name=menu-api-service
kubectl get svc web-service -n jahez-prod -o yaml

Debug

kubectl run tmp -n jahez-prod --rm -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot -- bash
dig +search menu-api-service
curl http://menu-api-service/healthz
curl http://<podIP>:8080/healthz   # bypass the Service
kubectl port-forward svc/menu-api-service 8080:80 -n jahez-prod

DNS names

<svc>                          same namespace
<svc>.<ns>                     other namespace
<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local   full name
<pod>.<headless-svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local
_<port>._<proto>.<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local   SRV

Ports

port        → what clients dial on the Service
targetPort  → container port (number or name)
nodePort    → 30000–32767 on every node
name        → required with 2+ ports

Types

ClusterIP     internal VIP (default)
NodePort      + port on every node
LoadBalancer  + cloud LB (NLB)
ExternalName  CNAME only
clusterIP: None  → Headless

Traffic

sessionAffinity: ClientIP        sticky by source IP
externalTrafficPolicy: Local     keep client IP, no hop
internalTrafficPolicy: Local     same-node only (drops!)
trafficDistribution: PreferSameZone   prefer zone

Gotchas

empty EndpointSlice = selector/readiness
create service sets selector app=<name>
clusterIP is immutable
balancing is per connection (gRPC!)
ExternalName needs a hostname, not an IP

Kubernetes Services · reference guide v3 · names follow the "ends with its kind" rule; pod names in diagrams are shortened.
